title: Design to Implementation Study for Development and Patient Validation of Paper-Based Toehold Switch Diagnostics
protocol: Scan the Zika genome to identify candidate regions for amplification that are approximately 200 nucleotides (nt) to 300 nt in length using NCBI/Nucleotide BLAST.
Compare identified regions against reference RNA sequences and select sites that remain highly conserved without homology with the human genome.
Select at least two sites to design synthetic toehold switch primers.
Use the selection criteria of Deiman et al. to generate pairs of forward and reverse primers for each candidate amplification region.
Ensure GC content is between 40% and 60%.
Set primer length to 20 to 24 nucleotides with a melting temperature above 41°C.
Avoid runs of four or more identical nucleotides in the sequence.
End the final 3' nucleotide with an A base.
Minimize secondary structure formation and dimer probability for primers.
Screen 8-10 primer pairs per target region.
Append T7 promoter sequence to the 5' end of forward primers.
Order designed primers as DNA oligos from a synthesis company.
Install NUPACK version 3.2 on a UNIX operating system using MATLAB.
Identify target sequences specific to the pathogen of interest for toehold switch designs.
Choose Zika target sequences from nucleic acid sequence-based amplicons.
Design and test nucleic acid sequence-based amplification primers or toehold switches based on user needs.
Screen toehold switches first if target regions are established from existing publications or diagnostic protocols.

Screen nucleic acid sequence-based amplification primers against the full genome to narrow down targets of choice while selecting for primer amplification efficiency if no established target regions exist.
Design nucleic acid sequence-based amplification primers focusing on highly conserved regions if multiple sequences for the pathogen are available.
Download and install MATLAB software on the computer.
Open MATLAB software and open (or create) a startup.m file in the default work folder.

Copy specific lines of code into the startup.m file to set up environment variables: NUPACKINSTALL = '/Users/[user_name]/.../nupack3.2.2'; setenv('NUPACKINSTALL',NUPACKINSTALL); setenv('PATH',[getenv('PATH'),sprintf(':%s/build/bin',NUPACKINSTALL)]).
Add the folder containing the nucleic acid design suite binaries to the PATH.
Open the numeric computing platform software.
Navigate to the design software folder.
Run the design algorithms accessible at the specified location.
Input the target sequences into the design_input_file.csv located in the input subfolder.
Ensure the inputs include Name, Outer sequence, Inner sequence, Temperature, Output name, and Output sequence.
If no priming sites are determined yet for the target, keep inner and outer sequences the same.
Save and close the updated spreadsheet.
Select parameters to use for the design function: toehold_switch_design_run(num_designs,input_file,options).
Set num_designs - the number of top designs for each target output by the software.
Order the toehold switch hairpin sequences as DNA oligos.
Assemble the ordered sequences with the reporter gene into fully functional switches.
Order necessary PCR primers for subsequent sensor assembly based on the chosen reporter protein.
Use a DNA oligo as the forward primer and the T7 terminator as the reverse primer in overlap extension PCR.
Utilize the pCOLADuet-LacZ plasmid as a template for the lacZ gene during PCR.
Ensure that any alternative templates contain the corresponding sequence and include the T7 terminator in the final construct.
Prepare solutions of synthetic DNA and reverse amplification primer at a concentration of 10 µM in nuclease-free water.
Assemble PCR reactions on ice according to the specified volumes and concentrations.
Place the assembled reactions in a thermal cycler.
Follow the cycling conditions listed for initial denaturation at 98 °C for 30 seconds.
Continue with further cycling conditions as per Table 3.
Analyze the PCR products on an agarose gel.
Purify the PCR products using a spin column-based kit and elute in 15-30 µL of nuclease-free water.
Quantify the purified DNA using a spectrophotometer.
Use molecular biology design software to modify synthetic trigger RNA templates.
Include an upstream T7 promoter sequence in the modified templates.
Design forward and reverse primers for amplifying the trigger sequence.
Order the designed sequences as DNA oligos.
Reconstitute the synthetic trigger DNA and amplification primers to 10 µM in nuclease-free water.
Assemble PCRs according to Table 2 using 0.5 μL of the trigger DNA ultramer.
Place PCR reactions in a thermal cycler and use cycling conditions listed in Table 3.
Use an extension time of 15 seconds for each cycle.
Assess quality and purify trigger PCR products as described.
Purified products can be directly used for initial toehold switch screening.
Assemble reaction components on ice according to Table 4.
Incubate in vitro transcription reactions at 37 °C for 4 h.
Add 70 µL of nuclease-free water, 10 µL of 10x DNase I Buffer, and 2 µL of RNase-free DNase I.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 15 min.
If not proceeding to step 5.4 immediately, add 50 mM EDTA to inactivate DNase I.
Heat inactivate DNase I at 65 °C for 10 min.
Perform denaturing polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis analysis on the IVT products (optional).
Purify the trigger IVT products using a column-based RNA cleanup kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Quantify the RNA concentration and purity using spectrophotometry.
Prepare a CPRG stock solution by dissolving 25 mg of the powder in 1 mL of nuclease-free water.
Keep the CPRG stock solution on ice at all times.
Store the CPRG stock solution at -20 °C for long-term use.
Determine the number of reactions to set up.
Include a no template control for each toehold switch assessed.
Add a switch only control to assess background signal.
Assemble a cell-free reaction master mix of solution A on ice according to the standard protocol listed in Table 5.
Assemble a cell-free reaction master mix of solution B on ice according to the standard protocol listed in Table 5.
Assemble a cell-free reaction master mix with RNase inhibitor on ice according to the standard protocol listed in Table 5.
Assemble a cell-free reaction master mix with CPRG on ice according to the standard protocol listed in Table 5.
Dispense the master mix into a PCR tube on ice.
Add nuclease-free water to 5.84 µL for the cell-free alone control and mix by pipetting up and down.
Centrifuge the cell-free alone control briefly.
Add PCR purified toehold switch DNA to a final concentration of 33 nM for the reaction tubes.
Add nuclease-free water to 5.84 µL for the switch alone controls.
Add in vitro transcribed target RNA to a final concentration of 1 µM for the toehold switch and target RNA combination tubes.
Add nuclease-free water to 5.84 µL for the tubes with target RNA added.
Mix all reactions thoroughly by pipetting up and down.
Centrifuge all reactions briefly.
Add 30 µL of nuclease-free water to the wells surrounding the reaction wells on a 384-well black, clear bottomed plate.
Using a 2 mm biopsy punch and tweezers, cut BSA-blocked filter paper disks.
Place the filter paper disks in reaction wells using tweezers.
Dispense triplicate 1.8 µL volumes from each reaction tube onto the filter paper discs.
Keep all samples on ice during dispensing.
Add 1.8 µL of CPRG (0.6 mg/mL) to each corner of a 384-well plate for portable plate reader alignment.
Cover the wells with PCR film to prevent evaporation.
Place the 384-well plate in a plate reader.
Read OD570 at 37 °C every minute for 130 minutes.
Normalize data by subtracting the OD570 measurements of reactions without any switch or target RNA from all other OD570 measurements.
Smooth the normalized data using a three-point moving average.
Adjust the minimum value of each well to zero.
Calculate the fold change (ON/OFF ratio) by determining the difference in the rate of color change between the toehold switch and target, and switch alone wells.
Select switches with the highest ON/OFF fold change for further characterization.
Omit poorly performing toehold switches that display the lowest fold change.
Make a 25 µM stock solution of all forward and reverse primer sets in nuclease-free water.
Determine the number of nucleic acid sequence-based amplification reactions needed.
Set up subsequent cell-free reactions based on the number of toehold switches and respective primer sets.
Include no template controls for each primer set during screening.
Thaw all reagents on ice.
Assemble a reaction master mix according to Table 6.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down until the white precipitate is solubilized.
Dispense aliquots into PCR tubes.
If screening nucleic acid sequence-based amplification primers, exclude the primers from the master mix.
Otherwise, if performing primer sensitivity analysis, include the primers in the master mix.
Add 2.55 µL of master mix without primers for primer set screening.
Dispense 2.75 µL aliquots including primers for primer sensitivity analysis.
Add enzyme mix after denaturation and equilibration stages.
If screening nucleic acid sequence-based amplification primers, add forward and reverse primers to appropriate tubes.
On a thermal cycler, set up the incubation protocol as described in Table 7.
Add 1 µL of nuclease-free water or target trigger RNA at 2 pM or approximately 106 copies/µL.
Label tubes accordingly.
Mix by gentle pipetting and briefly spin down the tubes.
Move the tubes to the thermal cycler and start the incubation.
After 12 min, remove the tubes from the thermal cycler.
Add 1.25 µL of the enzyme mix to each tube.
Mix by pipetting up and down.
Briefly centrifuge the tubes.
Keep the tubes at room temperature or return them to the thermal cycler for a 1 h reaction incubation after skipping the 41 °C hold step.
Place the reactions on ice for same-day processing or freeze them at -20 °C for later processing.
Assemble paper-based cell-free toehold switch reactions to assess primer performance as described in steps 6.2-6.7 and Table 8.
Analyze data according to steps 7.1-7.2 and Figure 3.
Include a negative control to account for background signal from the reaction.
Include a no-NASBA amplification control with the switch and 2 pM of target RNA.
Identify candidate primer pairs for sensitivity analysis.
Keep RNA samples on ice at all times.
Make a serial dilution set of target RNAs in nuclease-free water: 10^4, 10^3, 10^2, 10^1, and 10^0 RNA copies/µL.
Repeat nucleic acid sequence-based amplification with the selected primer sets.
Test the serial dilution series to identify the best sensitivity.
Confirm the reproducibility of results in biological triplicate before moving to experiments with patient samples.
Optionally, clone the selected switch sequence(s) into a plasmid for long-term use and transport.
Collect peripheral blood samples from suspected arbovirus-infected patients.
Perform venipuncture (whole blood tube) using a standard aseptic technique.
Label the sample tubes with an anonymous code and the date of sample collection.
Centrifuge blood to separate serum at 2,300 x g for 10 minutes.
Prepare aliquots of serum (200 µL) in 1.5 mL tubes for RNA extraction.
If immediate RNA extraction is not possible, store serum samples at -80 °C.
Pipette 560 µL of Buffer AVL into a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 140 µL of serum to the Buffer AVL/carrier RNA mixture.
Mix by pulse-vortexing for 15 seconds.
Incubate the sample for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge the sample briefly to collect contents at the bottom of the tube.
Add 560 µL of ethanol (96%-100%) to the sample.
Mix by pulse-vortexing for 15 seconds.
Centrifuge the sample to collect contents at the bottom of the tube.
Carefully add 630 µL of solution from step 9.4 to the spin-column without wetting the rim.
Close the cap, and centrifuge at 6,000 x g for 1 minute.
Place the spin-column into a clean 2 mL collection tube; discard used collection tube containing filtrate.
Open the spin-column carefully and repeat step 9.5.
Add 500 µL of Buffer AW1 to the open spin-column.
Close the cap, and centrifuge at 6,000 x g for 1 minute.
Place the spin-column into a clean 2 mL collection tube; discard used collection tube containing filtrate.
Carefully open the spin-column and add 500 μL of Buffer AW2 (wash buffer 2).
Close the cap and centrifuge at 20,000 x g for 3 min.
Place the spin-column into a clean 2 mL collection tube and discard the used collection tube containing the filtrate.
Place the spin-column into a clean 2 mL collection tube to avoid contamination by residual buffer AW2.
Centrifuge at 20,000 x g for 1 min.
Place the spin-column in a clean 1.5 mL tube and discard the used collection tube with the filtrate.
Carefully open the spin-column and add 60 μL of Buffer AVE (elution buffer) equilibrated to room temperature.
Close the cap, and incubate at room temperature for 1 min.
Centrifuge at 6,000 x g for 1 min.
Perform nucleic acid sequence-based amplification using 1 µL of extracted patient RNA.
Include negative and positive control reactions during amplification.
Prepare a 384-well reaction plate following the reactions.
Run the assay in the portable plate reader device at 37 °C.
Upload raw data (.csv file) from the plate reader to a secure database online.
Generate a report indicating whether samples are positive or negative for Zika virus.
Transfer files from the portable plate reader to your computer via USB.
Assemble RT-qPCR components in an area isolated from the amplification process.
Place RT-qPCR buffer, enzymes, and primer/probes on ice or a cold-block.
Add reactions to a 384-well plate on ice according to Table 9.
Mix reaction by pipetting up and down (do not vortex).
Dispense 6.5 μL into each well.
Add 3.5 μL of each RNA template in triplicate.
Place a PCR film over the top of the plate.
Centrifuge the 384-well plate at 600 x g for 2 min.
Place the plate in a RT-qPCR machine using the cycling conditions outlined in Table 10.
Analyze results using RT-qPCR machine design and analysis software.
Consider automatic threshold and baseline for analysis.
Reverse transcription at 45 °C for 15 min.
Perform PCR initial activation step at 95 °C for 5 min.
Denature the mixture at 95 °C for 5 s in each of 45 cycles.
Combine annealing and extension steps at 60 °C for 45 s in each of 45 cycles.
